item.title: The fans at the FA Cup game no-one could see
item.description: Ian Kirke struggled to watch his side's FA Cup first round match against Altrincham due to thick fog [Ian Kirke] For many football fans, an FA Cup win is the stuff of dreams. But for 690 Notts County supporters, thick fog meant they could barely see it happen. Ian Kirke was among the Magpies fans whose view of Saturday's FA Cup first-round tie against Altrincham was obscured by fog, leaving many unable to see the League One side's penalty shootout victory. The thick layer of fog provided chaos not just for the players and fans, but also commentators and camera operators at the J Davidson Stadium. Kirke said fans had to rely on the cheers - or silence - from the home support during the shootout. "It's the most bonkers festival of football I've ever seen in my life," he added. Heavy fog meant Notts County fans were unable to watch the penalty shootout that took place at the other end of the pitch [Getty Images] Lifelong fan Kirke, who lives in Berkshire, said the weather at kick-off was "like any normal match". Before fog descended over Greater Manchester, Jacob Bedeau had given Notts County the lead just before the half-hour mark. The hosts, who play in the National League, hit back as Lucas Weaver and Lewis Banks scored to give Altrincham a 2-1 lead. With the conditions worsening, referee David Rock opted to continue with the tie, which saw the camera often unable to pick up the ball. The referee's decision to continue the game paid off for Notts County, who levelled the tie at 2-2, when Callum Roberts scored from the edge of the box. "I can just about see the bright white numbers on their shirts, but I am struggling to see what is happening on the far side of the pitch," said BBC Radio Nottingham commentator Adam Hassell. Former Notts County striker Mark Stallard was also commentating on BBC Radio Nottingham, and said: "We're looking around, and here in the press box no-one knows where the ball is! It's like a spot the ball competition. "We genuinely cannot see the linesman or the players on the far side. It's slightly farcical having to commentate for radio listeners." Lynda Lally said the fog got worse during the second half [Dan Westwell] Fellow Magpies fan Lynda Lally, from Beeston in Nottinghamshire, said the weather got "worse and worse" after half-time. "For the other 45 minutes, we could only see what was happening once players emerged from the fog," she said. The weather became "a cross between an eerie Christmas nativity gone horribly wrong - and the 1980s film called The Fog," Kirke said. Kirke added the fog that led to an FA Cup third-round replay between Notts County and Wimbledon being abandoned in 2001 "wasn't as bad" as it was at Altrincham. item.description: Nov 9, 2026; Dallas, Texas, USA; Dallas Mavericks forward Cooper Flagg (32) celebrates making a three point shot during the second half against the Indiana Pacers at the American Airlines Center. Despite the inherent pressure of carrying a franchise at just 19 years old, it is safe to say that the Mavericks’ superstar has delivered. On the second night of a back-to-back, Cooper Flagg dropped a historic performance of 43 points, 10 rebounds, six assists, and three steals to lead the Mavericks to a clutch 125-122 victory over the Indiana Pacers . Aside from marking his fifth 40-point game, this stat line also sees him emerge as the first teenager to notch a 40/10/5/3 game in NBA history . Purely from an individual perspective, this is spectacular. However, the fact that it results in wins for the Mavericks is equally promising. On that note, during his postgame media availability , Cooper Flagg addressed his growing impact and how he has improved as a scorer in clutch situations. “It just speaks to the type of basketball I’ve always played and how I was raised being a true competitor,” Flagg shared about his impact. “Whenever I get out there on the court, it just goes back to being a competitor and trying to make as many winning plays as I can. I’m trying to make the easy, right basketball play out there. It just speaks to that. My teammates put me in good positions. My coaches trust me to go out there and make plays.” In the fourth quarter, Cooper Flagg scored the first basket to bring the Mavs level at 93-93. After this point, the 19-year-old went on a tear, notching a total of 16 points, which included the clutch basket to extend Dallas’ lead to four points with less than 30 seconds on the clock. Flagg’s poise and composure in these clutch situations speak volumes about his development in the brief span of one season. item.title: Victor Wembanyama reveals he wants to take the next step as a dominant center
item.description: Victor Wembanyama reveals he wants to take the next step as a dominant center originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . After a slow start to the 2026-27 NBA season, some people were hesitant to keep calling Victor Wembanyama the MVP favorite. Of course, he has returned to top form, as he is playing like the best player in the league at the moment. The San Antonio Spurs now have a 9-2 record after beating the Phoenix Suns on Monday. Wembanyama had yet another landmark performance, as he posted a stat line of 40 points, 11 rebounds, and nine blocks. Victor Wembanyama believes he's not the complete player just yet Despite having one of the best runs a center has had in the NBA this season, Wembanyama believes that he is not the finished article just yet. Of course, he is correct with that assessment, but it goes to show his elite mentality because he is already having some generational performances. The last four games, in particular, have been remarkable. He has only played 27.5 minutes per game during this stretch, but he is averaging 37.7 points and five blocks per game. It is an impressive look into his dominance and how he can decide games early on with his impact. MORE: Victor Wembanyama reveals the lesson he learned from Gregg Popovich Wembanyama has clearly cemented himself as one of the leading candidates for the MVP award alongside the Los Angeles Lakers ' Luka Doncic. The Slovenian might have the leg up in scoring and playmaking, but Wembanyama is matching him well with scoring and defending. Despite those strengths, it looks like Wembanyama still wants to keep improving. If he is already this good as an unfinished product, that spells trouble for the rest of the NBA. "There are a lot of things I still want to do, but I need to get better first. As the years go on and my conditioning gets better, it allows me to keep developing on both sides of the floor," Wembanyama said about what he needs to keep improving on moving forward . In the long run, Wembanyama will be an even more dangerous player. He has all the tools to become one of the league's best-ever players, and he wants to keep adding to his skill set. item.title: Coachella Valley's Chris Mañon scores career-high 32 points in win over San Diego
item.description: Coachella Valley Lakers guard Chris Mañon (30) goes up for a shot during an NBA G League basketball game against the Salt Lake City Stars, Friday, Nov. 6, 2026, at Acrisure Arena in Palm Desert, Calif. PALM DESERT, Calif. — Behind Chris Mañon’s career-high 32 points and 13 rebounds, the Coachella Valley Lakers started the season 2-0 after a 124-110 win over the San Diego Clippers on Monday night. Mañon set the tone early with 16 points in the first quarter. Mañon also added a steal and two blocks. His previous career high came almost a year to the day on Nov. 10, 2025, when he had 31 points against the Valley Suns. “I did know, I thought it was 33 but it was 31 last year. I could’ve had 40 tonight, but maybe tomorrow,” Mañon said postgame. “It's my bread and butter,” turning defense into offense, Mañon said. “Being that point of attack defender is something I take a lot of pride in on the defensive side.” The difference between this year and last year for Mañon has been his offensive output. “Just playing with more confidence, playing with joy, not being afraid to make mistakes,” Mañon said. For Mañon, he’s staying patient while on a two-way contract with the Lakers. He spoke about remaining patient throughout the process. Wikipedia “Just controlling what I can control. I'll say this, first half I was a little more patient, second half not so much. Ultimately, I think I can do a better job with my mentality.” When asked about Mañon’s career high in points scored, head coach Zack Cerda said it all started with his defense. “It really started with his defense, being a good point of attack defender. He’s just a tone setter for us on the defensive end. Offensively he’s able to attack closeouts. He makes good decisions, two-on-one reads in the paint, getting to the free-throw line. He’s a great downhill player, applying great pressure on the defense.” For Mañon, the focus has been on improving his shot. “He can shoot it,” Cerda said. “He’s been putting in a lot of time on his shot working with coach Liam Flynn.” Four of the five Lakers starters scored in double figures: Cole Swider added 21 points, Jahmir Young had 21 points, and Arthur Kaluma had 16 points on 6-of-12 shooting from the field. Coachella Valley dominated on the glass, outrebounding San Diego 49-30. 17 of the 49 rebounds were offensive. Cerda credited the team's practice drill called “Set the Tone” for their effective rebounding. “It looks like a football practice out there when we’re working on rebounding,” Cerda said. Mañon led the team with 13 rebounds. San Diego fell to 1-1 on the new season. The Clippers made three more field goals than Coachella Valley following a fourth-quarter scoring run that cut a 28-point lead down to 15. The Lakers tightened defense to close out the win. A quick turnaround for both teams as the second half of the back-to-back takes place Tuesday at 7 p.m. PST at Acrisure Arena.

item.title: ‘Like Rudy Gobert’ – NFL fans ruthlessly call out major Minnesota Vikings flaw after MNF loss
item.description: Photo by David Berding/Getty Images The Minnesota Vikings offence was exposed against the Buffalo Bills on Monday night, and fans online are letting them hear it. The Minnesota Vikings suffered their second straight loss after a 23-6 defeat to the Buffalo Bills on Monday night. Quarterback Carson Wentz had an extremely poor game, completing just 8 of 25 passes for 81 yards and throwing two interceptions. Buffalo’s defence made life miserable for Minnesota, they managed to limit Justin Jefferson to just three catches for 58 yards. James Cook rushed for 107 yards and a touchdown as the Bills pulled away in the second half, handing the Vikings just their second defeat of the year. NFL fans were not amused by watching the Minnesota Vikings offence struggle, but did make fun of them for it Minnesota began their campaign with a 6-0 run, but the problems with the offence have been a consistent theme. Their defence has limited teams significantly, allowing them to put up a run despite averaging less than 20 points per game as a team through their first eight games. Teams can get away with obvious flaws sometimes when the wins keep coming. After their second consecutive loss, though, it seems that fans have lost their patience with the Vikings. “The Minnesota Vikings are like if Rudy Gobert was an NFL team,” one fan hilariously said. “This is the most accurate comparison of all time lol,” another agreed. “The Vikings QB situation is so bad that Joe Buck & Troy Aikman are repairing their relationship by laughing at our QBs,” a third fan posted. “Vikings should be calling Bengals about Joe Flacco at this point,” a fourth fan claimed. “Lowest QBR in years the night before the trade deadline. That’s not a game, that’s a cry for help, fam,” a fifth fan said. “The Vikings deserve all this and more, some people were getting delusional after that 6-0 start,” a sixth fan commented. Gobert is known for being one of the most dominant defensive players in NBA history, but his offence leaves a lot to be desired. The Vikings being compared to the big man is both hilarious, and sadly true at the moment. The franchise really needs to address their quarterback situation, and quickly. item.title: Warriors Suffer Another Setback As Brandon Williams Could Miss Extended Time After Hamstring Injury
item.description: SAN FRANCISCO, CA - NOVEMBER 7: Brandon Williams #12 of the Golden State Warriors handles the ball during the game against the Orlando Magic on November 7, 2026 at Chase Center in San Francisco, California. (Photo by Jed Jacobsohn/NBAE via Getty Images) The Golden State Warriors faced the New Orleans Pelicans tonight and destroyed them 138-87 at the Chase Center in San Francisco. But early in the first quarter, they faced another injury setback when Brandon Williams left for the locker room with less than four minutes left, after scoring four points on 2-for-3 shooting (66.7% FG). The 26-year-old guard did not return for the rest of the night, joining players like Jimmy Butler , Will Richard, and Moses Moody on the Warriors’ extended injury list. The team later announced it has scheduled an MRI for tomorrow, November 10, to better understand the extent of the issue before suggesting any timeline for his return. “As per Warriors’ PR, Brandon Williams will undergo an MRI on his left hamstring. If Williams misses extended time, that’s another blow to the Warriors’ backcourt depth with Will Richard also out,” wrote ClutchPoints’ Warriors reporter, Kenzo Fukuda, on X. Williams has been coming off the bench and consistently been impactful for the Warriors. He has averaged 10.4 points, 2.3 assists, and 2.1 rebounds while shooting 41.3% from the field and 30.4% from beyond the arc. This will be another setback for a roster already plagued by injuries. “It’s a big concern; he’s a huge part of our team. And he’s given us a lift. It’s a hamstring thing; we’ll get an MRI, and we’ll see how that is,” head coach Steve Kerr said during the postgame press conference. L.J. Cryer played extended minutes in Williams’ absence as Golden State extended their winning streak to eight games and improved to 8-3 for the season. Veterans like Draymond Green and Stephen Curry played only 21 minutes each tonight, a silver lining in a low-effort night for the Warriors. They have plenty of reasons to feel confident after extending their winning streak to eight games, but Brandon Williams’ injury is an unfortunate development that could complicate their rotation. item.title: Warriors Player Ratings: Curry Drops An Efficient 25 To Blow Out Pelicans In Lopsided Matchup
item.description: Mandatory Credit: Kelley L Cox-Imagn Images The Golden State Warriors delivered an absolute demolition of the New Orleans Pelicans , cruising to a 138-87 victory behind an explosive offensive performance. Stephen Curry finished with 25 points on efficient shooting (6-10), but he wasn’t even the Warriors’ leading scorer in a game where the entire rotation was scorching hot. Yaxel Lendeborg and Brandin Podziemski each scored 25 points, combining for 19-29 shooting from the field. Lendeborg was particularly impressive, knocking down all four of his three-point attempts while contributing seven rebounds and four assists. Podziemski matched the scoring total with five triples of his own. Golden State shot an incredible 54.9% from the field and 47.7% from three-point range, compared to New Orleans’ miserable 36.3% and 28.6%, respectively. The Warriors also dominated the glass 50-31, dished out 37 assists, and finished with a staggering 51-point largest lead. Here are the Warriors’ player ratings from the blowout victory. Stephen Curry: A+ Game Stats: 25 PTS, 5 REB, 2 AST, 1 TOV, 6-10 FG, 4-7 3-PT FG, 9-9 FT, 21 MIN Curry was incredibly efficient, scoring 25 points in just 21 minutes while shooting 60.0% from the field and making four three-pointers. He also converted all nine free throws, barely wasting a scoring opportunity. The Warriors didn’t need Curry to play extended minutes, and the superstar made the most of his time on the floor. An efficient scoring performance with minimal turnovers is exactly what Golden State wants from its leader. Yaxel Lendeborg: A+ Game Stats: 23 PTS, 7 REB, 4 AST, 1 STL, 2 TOV, 8-10 FG, 4-4 3-PT FG, 3-4 FT, 27 MIN Lendeborg was spectacular. He finished with 23 points on just 10 shot attempts, including a perfect 4-4 performance from beyond the arc. His efficiency was remarkable, and he contributed seven rebounds and four assists along the way. Golden State received a tremendous two-way performance from Lendeborg, who finished with a team-high +34. This was precisely the kind of performance that makes a blowout even more convincing. Brandin Podziemski: A+ Game Stats: 25 PTS, 2 REB, 4 AST, 1 STL, 1 BLK, 10-19 FG, 5-11 3-PT FG, 26 MIN Podziemski matched Curry’s scoring total while taking on a larger offensive workload. His five three-pointers helped Golden State completely overwhelm New Orleans from the perimeter. Although he wasn’t quite as efficient as Lendeborg, Podziemski’s 25 points and four assists were instrumental in the offensive explosion. Zero turnovers made his performance even better. Al Horford: A- Game Stats: 5 PTS, 2 REB, 6 AST, 2 STL, 3 BLK, 2-5 FG, 1-3 3-PT FG, 15 MIN Horford was outstanding defensively and as a facilitator. Six assists, two steals, and three blocks in only 15 minutes represent an impressive all-around contribution. He also knocked down a three-pointer, helping maintain Golden State’s offensive spacing. Horford’s versatility was on full display in this dominant performance. Charles Basse

item.title: Nixa soccer gets revenge over bogey team Glendale in district championship
item.description: SPRINGFIELD — Revenge is a dish best served cold. On a chilly evening, Nixa soccer bested Glendale 1-0 behind a late goal to lift the Class 4 district championship on Monday, Nov. 9. This was Nixa’s first victory over Glendale since 2023, after losing five straight games. It’s a moment that many of the seniors have been dreaming of, especially goalkeeper Jackson Smith. “It feels great, senior year, we haven’t beat them since freshman year,” Smith said. “For us to come out and win a district championship, it feels good for our city, our team. I’m thrilled.” Smith had a stellar game, but when a hero was needed, Gavin Shaw rose to the occasion. Cross country: Gloria Deo's Caroline Fields wins Class 1 state title with sister by her side With three minutes remaining, Shaw received the ball on the left wing. The senior danced on the ball a few times, juking out Glendale’s defense. He drove towards the byline before firing a cross. The ball ricocheted off of a Glendale defender and snuck through the goal at the near post. “It’s definitely a top momentum of my life,” Shaw said. “Scoring a game-winner in the district championship is always fun. Run to the corner and have everyone jump in and celebrate, it was super exciting.” It wasn’t the prettiest goal, but it was a testament to Nixa’s style of play. The Eagles wanted the ball down the wings and it’s where they made the most of their chances. Nixa fired cross after cross into Glendale’s box throughout the match. The variety of crosses made it difficult for Glendale. They were sometimes pinged to the six-yard line, or they were lofted to the back post. Each cross proved that Nixa was getting closer to a goal, finally hitting the back of the net with minutes to spare. “We moved our wings up the field. We wanted to make sure we’re defensively solid, but then get up and attack,” Nixa head coach Evan Palmer said. “It puts Gavin and Spencer (Rinne), who play the wing a lot, up there where they can do their stuff because they’re fantastic on the ball.” High school football: Breaking down Springfield area district semifinal action Shaw’s goal was the difference maker. The celebrations wouldn't happen without Smith’s strong wrists. He was called into action on multiple occasions, showcasing his reflexes and stopping ability. Glendale attacked down Nixa’s left wing with 10 minutes to play. A shot was fired and Shaw needed to fully extend himself to cover the back post. It was a fantastic save, but the ball filtered to the top of the box. Glendale’s next shot rattled the bar before Nixa could clear the lines. It was one of the Falcons’ best chances of the game. “I couldn’t even tell you,” Shaw said, reliving the close call. “I freaked out. I was happy, but I tried not to get too happy. I try to stay consistent and stay in the zone, but it’s hard not to get excited.” Glendale has been Nixa’s bogey team for years. In the regular season, the Falcons won 3-2. In the district championship, Nixa got its moment to shine.

item.description: Photo by Michael Reaves/Getty Images Skip Bayless has aimed yet another dig at LeBron James, this time following the Los Angeles Lakers’ 124-114 win against the Atlanta Hawks. That shows just how good a side they are, and Bayless has used this to criticise James without even naming him. Skip Bayless says the Los Angeles Lakers don’t miss LeBron James James spent eight years with the Los Angeles Lakers and helped them win the 2020 NBA Championship. The King had his ups and downs with the team, but when he was at his best, he was exceptional and among the very best players the NBA had ever seen. Yet, many people like Bayless have constantly had a go at James for his shortcomings during his time with the Lakers. Even though it has been a few months since he left Los Angeles and joined the Philadelphia 76ers, some of them still fire shots at James while speaking about the Lakers. He tweeted after their win against the Hawks: “The Los Angeles Lakers now have the NBA’s best record. No, they do not miss him.” That last line is unnecessary, in our opinion, but the Lakers deserve huge credit for the way they have performed in the opening 12 games of the season, winning 10. There were a few concerns when James left, and some people even felt they weren’t strong enough to compete with the big teams this season. Cox) Luka Doncic scored 32 points as the in-form Los Angeles Lakers rolled to a sixth straight victory with a 124-114 defeat of the Atlanta Hawks on Monday. Doncic, whose sensational early season form has propelled the Lakers to the top of the NBA Western Conference, once again led from the front to secure an impressive win on the road. The Slovenian star finished with 32 points, 10 assists, eight rebounds, five steals and two blocks in a dominant all round performance. Doncic, who is averaging 40 points per game so far this season, received offensive support from Sandro Mamukelashvili, who delivered an eye-catching 23 points from the bench that included five three-pointers. Walker Kessler added 21 points with Collin Sexton scoring 18 and Ziaire Williams 12. Lakers coach J.J. Redick paid tribute to the contributions of Doncic, Sexton and Mamukelashvili on a night when the team were missing Austin Reaves (illness) and Quentin Grimes (injury). "I thought Collin did a really nice job of giving us some juice and Sandro had his best game as a Laker," Redick said. "That was awesome. "Luka, again, just orchestrating. He was out there without a secondary ball handler so he had to be on the ball a lot and that was taxing. I thought he handled it well," Redick added. The Lakers improved to 10-2 at the top of the Western Conference following the win as Atlanta fell to 7-5. The San Antonio Spurs meanwhile maintained their hot pursuit of the Lakers in the West, extending their winning streak to nine games after blowing out the Phoenix Suns 122-96 on the road to improve to 9-2. Usman Khawaja's autobiography has revived one of cricket’s most painful and divisive scandals. In a latest video, Khawaja has responded to critics who questioned his motives for telling the story. Did Australian bowlers know about Sandpapergate? Mitchell Starc responds to Usman Khawaja Mitchell Starc has made it clear that the Australian bowlers weren’t aware of any sandpaper plan in 2018, and he has no intention of changing that account now. The left-arm quick was responding to Usman Khawaja’s autobiography, which claims that every member of the touring team knew what was being planned during the Cape Town Test. Starc was speaking at the Kayo Sports and Fox Cricket season launch, where he was asked about the claims. He did not hide the fact that he had paid little attention to the debate, but he was firm on the one point that matters to him, which is that his memory of the events has not shifted in the slightest. The background to his stance is a joint statement released in 2021, after Cameron Bancroft gave an interview to The Guardian that raised fresh doubts about the official version of events. Starc, along with Nathan Lyon, Josh Hazlewood and Pat Cummins, said at the time that none of the four bowlers had known about the use of sandpaper on the ball. However, Khawaja's book has now contradicted that statement, and it has pushed an old controversy back into the headlines. “Yeah, that’s the first I was aware of any of that taking place in PE (second Test) was when (Khawaja said it) … I’ll leave that for said authors to explain,” Starc said. He went on to admit that he had not followed the discussion closely, and he pointed out that opinions from eight years ago were bound to differ. “I haven’t really paid much attention to be fair, obviously there’s differing opinions of eight years ago," he said. "We were heavily drilled through the process at the time, and since and I guess I won’t speak on behalf of the bowlers, but where I stand, my opinion hasn’t changed. My recollection hasn’t changed from what we said in 2021." His final remarks drew a narrow line around what the joint statement actually covered, which was the question of whether the bowlers knew anything was being taken onto the field. “As far as our statement said, we weren’t aware of things being taken on the field, that’s where I’ll leave it.” More to follow...

Kyriacou, 61, has had an indelible impact on the Oakland community through four decades as a coach, educator and leader - just like Beam, the legendary former Skyline High and Laney College coach and athletic director who died last November. Kyriacou described Beam as a big brother, a mentor, a friend and a colleague all wrapped in one. Beam and Kyriacou grew up together in the Oakland high school sports scene, and although they spent only seven years on the same staff at Skyline High, the pair worked hand-in-hand to shape countless lives over almost 40 years. The San Antonio Spurs have gotten their season off to a strong start, and a big reason for that is their big man out of France. Led by Victor Wembanyama, the Spurs have won eight of their first 10 games to start the 2026-27 regular season, and lead the Phoenix Suns by 15 at the half on Monday night. Through his first 10 games played this season, Victor Wembanyama is averaging 29.1 points, 12.0 rebounds, 3.0 assists, 1.2 steals, and 3.9 blocks per game while shooting 50.5 percent from the field.
